<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914059_theRebbe_310" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914059_theRebbe_310__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the header information for the maamar, including the Torah portion and date.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbos Parshas Haazinu,</t>
    <t s="2">Shabbos Teshuvah,</t>
    <t s="3">the year 5737*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section questions the redundancy of the verse, since "Return, O Israel" already implies verbal confession, and asks why "Take words with you" and "return to Hashem" are added.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"Return, O Israel, to Hashem your G-d... Take words with you and return to Hashem."1</t>
    <t s="1">And it needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="2">that when it says "Return, O Israel," the intention is repentance as it should be,</t>
    <t s="3">and since it is a positive commandment to confess</t>
    <t s="4">(when one repents)2,</t>
    <t s="5">to the extent that confession is among the essentials of repentance3,</t>
    <t s="6">then "Return, O Israel" also includes verbal confession,</t>
    <t s="7">so what is added by "Take words with you"?4</t>
    <t s="8">Likewise, the continuation "and return to Hashem" must be explained,</t>
    <t s="9">for from this it is implied that after the repentance of "Return, O Israel,"</t>
    <t s="10">there needs to be yet another repentance.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains two interpretations of "until" in the verse: one referring to making Hashem your G-d, and another referring to a level above the chain of descent, with two sub-levels of "until."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood by prefacing what was explained above5,</t>
    <t s="2">that what is written "Return, O Israel, until Hashem your G-d"</t>
    <t s="3">(even though ostensibly it should have said "to Hashem your G-d"),</t>
    <t s="4">is,</t>
    <t s="5">according to the explanation of the Alter Rebbe6,</t>
    <t s="6">that the repentance must be until Hashem becomes your G-d.</t>
    <t s="7">And there is another explanation7</t>
    <t s="8">regarding "Return, O Israel, until,"</t>
    <t s="9">that "until" refers to a level above that which is called "until"8.</t>
    <t s="10">And also in this there are two levels,</t>
    <t s="11">"until and including" and "until but not including."</t>
    <t s="12">"Until and including" is</t>
    <t s="13">(generally)</t>
    <t s="14">in the levels within the order of the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="15">where all the levels in the chain of descent are relative to one another,</t>
    <t s="16">therefore,</t>
    <t s="17">even when one is in a lower level, he already has a connection to the levels above it,</t>
    <t s="18">and up to the highest level,</t>
    <t s="19">"until and including."</t>
    <t s="20">And "until but not including" is in that which is above the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="21">for even when one is in the highest level within the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="22">he will not thereby reach the level that is above the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="23">"until but not including."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
